To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) online shopping is a complementary, not adversarial, behavior with in store shopping; 2) the built environment, in store attributes, attitudes and lifestyles are important factors in online shopping behavior; 3) online shopping is more popular among young and educated people who are familiar with the internet and have a higher income.
online shopping has a positive impact on in store shopping and vice versa.
online shopping is a complementary, rather a substitute, to in store shopping.

the role of online shopping as a substitute for in store shopping trips.

the online shopping is a complement to in store retailing, not a substitute.

the emergence of online options in shopping related travel behaviors in Iran is an inevitable process that is likely to increase shopping related travel frequencies, and the in store shopping is still a preferred option for the Iranian consumers, and online options are not a complete substitute to in store shopping.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
online shopping has become a significant shopping option for Iranians, but the growth of online shopping is not necessarily associated with a decline in in store shopping.
in store shopping and online shopping are two complementary shopping behaviors, and the growth of one does not necessarily lead to the decline of the other, especially in the developing countries.
the online shopping is not a substitute for the in store shopping, but a complementary one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ICT alternatives are not a one size fits all solution to reduce travel related to shopping.
in store and online shopping frequencies have complementary relationships.
the built environment, shopping attributes, and consumers' attitudes and lifestyles are the key determinants of shopping related travel behavior in Iran, as in other countries.
